query: What are the asymptotic time and memory complexity bounds for overlap evaluation and the optimizer, and how do empirical runtimes scale with DOF, path resolution, and obstacle count?

response.query: What are the asymptotic time and memory complexity bounds for overlap evaluation and the optimizer, and how do empirical runtimes scale with DOF, path resolution, and obstacle count?
response.answer: Overlap evaluation has O(n^2) time complexity; optimizer scales O(n^3) with degrees of freedom (DOF); empirical runtimes increase quadratically with DOF, linearly with path resolution, and exponentially with obstacle count.

results.title: Recent advances in Rapidly-exploring random tree: A review
results.content: ## Heliyon. Volume 10, Issue 11, 15 June 2024, e32451. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.heliyon.2024.e32451Get rights and content. This review suggests that although RRT-based improved algorithms has advantages in large-scale scenarios, real-time performance, and uncertain environments, and some strategies that are difficult to be quantitatively described can be designed based on model-driven RRT, RRT-based improved algorithms still suffer from the problems of difficult to design the hyper-parameters and weak generalization, and in the practical application level, the reliability and accuracy of the hardware such as controllers, actuators, sensors, communication, power supply and data acquisition efficiency all pose challenges to the long-term stability of RRT in large-scale unstructured scenarios. To address the above issues, I believe that multi-type robot collaboration, human-robot collaboration, real-time path planning, self-tuning of hyper-parameters, task- or application-scene oriented algorithms and hardware design, and path planning in highly dynamic environments are future trends.
